facts.existing_build_connected_family_scope: Build-level source groups conservatively connect entire repositories and declared/shared-key families; mlx-serve and Sushi always connect.

interpretation: The prior corpus builder explicitly protected the whole llama.cpp repository, not only individual reserved commits. This policy is a real artifact and must remain intact for the frozen active198/16 experiment.
The current candidate passes exact reserved head/base, declared PR and prior stable-patch screens. No exact contamination has been found by that finite screen.
Repository grouping is a conservative evaluation design, not proof that every newer llama.cpp optimization duplicates a protected task. No universal semantic overlap claim is justified.

Admitting non-overlapping newer llama.cpp edits to a future dataset would require a separately reviewed split policy and explicit removal of cross-repository-generalization claims for that new experiment; it must not alter existing heldout examples or retroactively relabel the active run.
Before any such future admission, compare complete selected kernel/context/patch with protected task units and declared related PRs; absence of an exact SHA match alone is insufficient.
next_action: Keep candidate in archive for now; parent can design a future finite lineage split after direct source-unit comparison. Do not permanently ban collection from llama.cpp.
